findings.reason: The protected source compresses paths but always attaches right_root below left_root. Path compression without union by rank or size does not justify its claimed inverse-Ackermann union-find bound, so the mismatch is material under an expert interview review. The inert candidate adds explicit component sizes and always attaches the smaller component below the larger one while preserving the app contract and output construction. The protected app source, immutable Accepted native source, and submission manifest remain unchanged.

The candidate is concise, conventional union-find code with descriptive parent, size, groups, choices, and root names. Initialization stays inside find, weighted union is explicit, component sorting and Cartesian-product generation each have one clear role, and no code golf, prohibited index binding, unnecessary abstraction, or surprising side effect obscures the reasoning.

Union-find merges exactly the endpoints of every undirected equivalence pair, so two synonym strings have the same representative exactly when they belong to the same connected component. Each component list is sorted once. Every text word then receives either that complete sorted list or the singleton original word; product chooses independently at every position. Its left-to-right enumeration over ascending choices yields all and only valid sentences in lexicographic order, including transitive replacements and repeated occurrences.

An independent adjacency-list/BFS oracle built connected components without union-find and generated results with recursive backtracking. It, the protected app source, immutable native source, weighted-union candidate, and an independently structured graph-plus-product control agreed on all twelve visible cases, all three final benchmark tiers, 9,920 exhaustive graph/text inputs over every graph on four synonym words, and 10,000 deterministic schema-valid random inputs generated with seed 1258. No implementation mutated either input.

The random corpus included 5,247 inputs with a transitive component, 6,797 with a repeated text word, 5,990 with a word outside the synonym graph, 2,059 with every position replaceable, 2,192 with zero pairs, 2,788 with no replaceable position, and 1,000 with disconnected components; output was capped at 4,096 sentences. Separate exact boundaries covered ten pairs, a ten-word sentence, ten-character synonym strings, and an eleven-word transitive chain formed by the maximum pair count.

The legacy tiers used pair counts 2, 4, and 8 as size even though returned-output count K is the required-complexity driver, and those small tiers rejected an independently correct same-class control because fixed Python overhead distorted relative growth. The final hidden tiers define size as K = 256, 512, and 1024 using eight, nine, and ten independent pairs, spanning 4x while remaining within every authenticated limit. In three repeated real-test runs, protected, candidate, and independent graph-plus-product controls passed every output and scaling. A correct reverse-generation plus custom mergesort O(K log K) control passed all fifteen outputs but failed only scaling each time, with extra-growth exponents +0.36 through +0.39 and largest runtime ratios 14.93x through 15.10x.

The exact second source example replaced an invented third sample, the two hidden correctness rows became visible trials, and the remaining invented sample rows were correctly reclassified as trials. Five additional visible cases cover a later bridge merging components, three independent occurrences of one word, equivalence from the second endpoint, the maximum pair count, and maximum synonym-string length. All twelve ordinary cases are now visible samples or trials.

Fresh authenticated evidence confirms unique pairs of distinct one-to-ten-character strings, zero through ten pairs, at most ten single-space-separated text words, transitive synonym groups, unrestricted choices at every replaceable position, and a lexicographically sorted result.

The protected solve.py and immutable leetcode.py remain byte-for-byte bound to verified submission 2068020549.
